story: Diarrhea Planet formed in Nashville in 2009 as a six-piece with four guitarists, and signed to Infinity Cat. Loose Jewels came out in 2011 and I'm Rich Beyond Your Wildest Dreams in 2013, which got them named one of Paste's Best of What's Next. They played Pickathon in 2014, the year of the Aliens in the Outfield EP, as a joyful four-guitar shred-fest. They announced a breakup on July 23, 2018, and played three farewell shows at the Exit/In that September. Reunion shows were announced in August 2022, and they still play celebratory hometown shows, as at Marathon Music Works and Eastside Bowl.

intro: A Portland band of jangly, laid-back guitar rock.
story: Houndstooth formed in Portland in 2010 as a five-piece, played their first show in May 2011 and put out a 7-inch that year. Ride Out the Dark came out on No Quarter on July 16, 2013, and they played Pickathon the next summer. No News from Home followed, and it is the last album on their discography.
artist_reel_line: No News from Home is the last record in their discography.

intro: A Louisiana accordionist of Creole dance-floor energy.
story: Leroy Thomas was born in 1965 and raised in Elton, Louisiana, the son of the zydeco drummer and bandleader Leo "The Bull" Thomas. He formed the Zydeco Roadrunners in 1998, and they played Pickathon in 2014, including its Pumphouse Sessions, which WWOZ filmed. We Love You Leroy! came out on Maison de Soul on August 4, 2015, and Rockin' the Bayou followed nearly a decade later. He plays Vermilionville in Lafayette, standing for classic Creole zydeco in Acadiana.

intro: A Northwest indie-rock band of scruffy melodies.
story: Sam Jayne formed Love As Laughter in 1994 as a solo project after the Seattle band Lync ended. The records came out on K and Sub Pop, among them Laughter's Fifth in 2005, and Holy followed in 2008 on Isaac Brock's Glacial Pace label. They played Pickathon in 2014. Sam Jayne died on December 15, 2020, at 46, and writers and fans still return to Laughter's Fifth.

Mikal Cronin was best known early on as the bass player in Ty Segall's band; his self-titled solo debut came out in 2011 on Trouble in Mind. Merge approached him after a South by Southwest set, he said, and he was blown away. MCII, his first for the label, came out May 7, 2013, with Ty Segall guesting, and Pitchfork named a track from it Best New Track the week of release. He played Pickathon in 2014. Seeker came out in 2019, and he played East Coast club dates in the spring of 2026.

intro: An Appalachian fiddle and banjo band.
story: Old Buck is a Portland bluegrass and old-time string band. At Pickathon in 2014 they led the festival's square dance with the caller Caroline Oakley, and were filmed in the Lucky Barn for The Bluegrass Situation, playing old-time tunes. Quip Magazine described the quartet entertaining a rapt crowd, with banjo and upright bass, in the campgrounds that August.
artist_reel_line: They led the festival square dance with caller Caroline Oakley.

intro: A Boston psych-folk quartet of sunlit harmonies.
story: Quilt began as a Boston trio of visual-arts students, Anna Fox Rochinski, Shane Butler and John Andrews, who met at the School of the Museum of Fine Arts. Held in Splendor, their second album, came out on Mexican Summer on January 28, 2014, produced by Jarvis Taveniere of Woods, and NPR's first listen said every song seems to knit together three distinct tunes. They played Pickathon that summer. Plaza followed on Mexican Summer in 2016, and the band has been inactive since the late 2010s.

intro: A psych-soul trio from three bands.
story: Spanish Gold paired Patrick Hallahan, the drummer of My Morning Jacket, with Dante Schwebel and Adrian Quesada of Grupo Fantasma. Their debut, South of Nowhere, came out May 27, 2014, on BMG/Del Mar. They played Forecastle on July 19, then Pickathon, and ACL Fest in October. South of Nowhere is their one album.
artist_reel_line: South of Nowhere was their one album.

intro: A Port Townsend jug and string-band duo.
story: Kit Stovepipe, a 78rpm collector, and the tenor banjoist Calliope Kane, who also goes by Windy City Alex, formed the Crow Quill Night Owls in 2007 in Port Townsend, Washington. They play the jug band, ragtime and hillbilly music of the 1920s and 30s. Kane has said that in that era many bands played the same songs and it was not called covering; the creativity is in the arrangement. KEXP's Roadhouse noted their new record in June 2013, and Grist filmed them at Pickathon in 2014 and picked "Crying My Blues Away" as its best breakup song.
artist_reel_line: Grist filmed them at the farm and picked their best breakup song.

intro: A San Diego band of sun-bleached coastal rock.
story: The Donkeys formed in San Diego in 2004 as a quartet and have not changed lineup since; they won Best Rock Band at the San Diego Music Awards in 2012. Ride the Black Wave, their fourth album, came out June 3, 2014, on Easy Sound, their first record away from Dead Oceans, where they made three. Relix called it a self-questioning fourth album. They played Pickathon that summer. In July 2025 they released La danza dei Serpenti.

Pete Krebs, of Hazel and the Oregon Music Hall of Fame class of 2013, and Leslie Beia met in the summer of 2014, and their first gig as the Earnest Lovers was a surprise Pickathon appearance. OPB listed them among the festival's musicians sharing summer songs in 2015, and noted they played Saturdays at Podnah's Pit. Krebs remains a longtime fixture of the Portland scene.

Jessi Zazu, Nikki Kvarnes and Kelley Anderson met at the Southern Girls Rock and Roll Camp in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, which Anderson founded in 2003, and formed Those Darlins in 2006. Their self-titled debut came in 2009 and Screws Get Loose, on Oh Wow Dang, on March 29, 2011; Robert Christgau on NPR heard "hooky, saucy, punky songwriting." Blur the Line followed in 2013, and they played Pickathon in 2014. The band broke up in 2016 after final shows, and its records carry the spirit of the late Jessi Zazu.

intro: A former Old Crow Medicine Show singer, solo and old-time.
story: Willie Watson was born in Watkins Glen, New York, in 1979 and co-founded Old Crow Medicine Show in Boone, North Carolina, leaving in 2011. David Rawlings produced Folk Singer Vol. 1, on Acony on May 6, 2014, over two two-day sessions at Woodland Sound in Nashville. He played Pickathon that summer. Folk Singer Vol. 2 came in September 2017, he plays in the Dave Rawlings Machine and at Newport Folk, and in late 2024 he released a self-titled album of original songs.

intro: A Brooklyn folk-rock band with tape-hissed jams.
story: Jeremy Earl, a native of Warwick, New York, formed Woods in Brooklyn in 2005, and also runs the Woodsist label. Jarvis Taveniere engineers the records, and both had been in Meneguar. Bend Beyond, written and recorded upstate in Warwick, came out on Woodsist on September 18, 2012, and With Light and With Love followed in 2014, the year of their Pickathon set. Stereogum later wrote about how Woods became an indie institution by staying DIY. Their last studio album, Perennial, came out in 2023.
